title: Monterey Wharf II Weekly Phytoplankton Monitoring Sample Collection and Processing
author: april woods
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.hiub4ew
materials: The following samples are processed and archived for later analysis: Nutrients: Whole water is passed through a 0.2 µm syringe filter and stored at -20°C Nucleic Acids: 50 mLs of the net tow sample are filtered through 1.2µm Isopore membrane filter (Millipore) and extracted into Trizol (Invitrogen) before being archived at -80°C. Protein and Amino Acids: 50mLs of the net tow are filtered through 2µm Isopore membrane filter (Millipore) and extracted into 80% Methanol before being archived at -80°C. Pigment: 25mLs of the net tow are filtered through Glass Microfibre Filters (Whatman) and archived at -80°C.

steps.title: Collect vertical net tow
steps.instruction: Perform a vertical net tow at a depth of 5 m using a 25µm mesh plankton net equipped with a 200mL cod-end piece.

steps.title: Collect vertical whole water samples
steps.instruction: Collect vertical whole water samples using a VanDorn at discrete 1m intervals, integrated over 5m.

steps.title: Estimate total phytoplankton biomass
steps.instruction: Estimate total phytoplankton biomass by measuring in vivo chlorophyll fluorescence of dark-adapted net and whole water samples using a calibrated Aquaflor fluorometer (Turner Designs).

steps.title: Assess species relative abundance
steps.instruction: Assess species relative abundance microscopically using 1% glutaraldehyde preserved samples quantified on a nanoplankton counting chamber (Phycotech).
